alt: Photo of people working together. Text: Most startups die from bad foundations, not bad ideas.
Chat: Roland, why do so many startups die early? 🧱 Usually not because of the idea. Thiel's law: a startup messed up at its foundation can't be fixed later.
Chat: Foundation like how? Co-founders first 🤝 Start with people you have real history with. Then agree in writing: who owns what, who decides, who's full-time.
Chat: I know, money and paperwork talk feels awkward with friends 😬 But it's far more awkward later. Have the talk early.
Chat: Your team 🧩 Hire people who'd love working together on a mission they believe in. Give each person one clear job, so nobody fights over the same work.

Chat: And if the product is really good, people will just come, right? 😅 That's one of the most expensive myths in business. If you can't reach customers at a cost you can afford, a great product still dies.
Chat: Match your selling to the deal size 💰 Big contracts: you, the founder, in the room. Small purchases: marketing, referrals, word of mouth. The middle is the hardest.
Chat: The 7 questions ✅ Engineering · Timing · Monopoly · People Distribution · Durability · Secret Which one is your business weakest on? Tell me 👇
